candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 20 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 21 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 22 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 23 not required. 24
candidates.context: The purpose of this guidance is to provide recommendations to sponsors regarding clinical trial 16 design features that can support approval of drugs and biological products intended for the 17 treatment of Fabry disease (FD). 2

candidates.statement: All eligible patients should have a confirmed diagnosis of FD based on both biochemical testing 81 and molecular genetic testing (as outlined below). Of note, both plasma and leukocyte α-Gal A 82 activity should be assayed given that some pathogenic GLA variants affect intracellular 83 trafficking and secretion of α-Gal A such that the reduction in α-Gal A enzyme activity in plasma 84 may be more pronounced than within leukocytes. Clinical trials should allow enrollment of both 85 male and female patients. As early as feasible, sponsors should consider enrolling pediatric 86 patients with FD in clinical trials. 87

candidates.statement: Given the rarity of FD, sponsors can use a single adequate and well-controlled trial (as described 114 in 21 CFR 314.126), showing a clinically meaningful treatment effect on core clinical aspects of 115 FD, as the basis for drug approval when accompanied by confirmatory evidence. A parallel- 116 group design should be used with an appropriate concurrent control group (placebo or active 117 treatment). Sponsors should consider stratifying at randomization by known prognostic factors, 118 such as sex and age. If the drug is intended to slow or arrest disease progression but not reverse 119 it, the trial should be of sufficient duration to observe disease progression in the control group. 120 There are special considerations regarding the length of long-term follow up for gene therapy 121 products. 12

candidates.statement: Demonstration of clinical benefit on any core disease manifestation (e.g., renal disease, 130 cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, gastrointestinal symptoms, neuropathic 131 symptoms, pain) can be the basis for traditional approval. 13 When selecting efficacy endpoints, 132 the sponsor should consider the natural history and time course of the selected disease 133 manifestation(s) assessed, the drug’s mechanism of action and the target organ(s), and the target 134 FD patient population or subpopulation. For instance, certain clinical outcome assessments may 135 not be appropriate for use in pediatric FD patients based on their age or symptom presence or 136 absence or severity. Similarly, classic FD and late-onset FD patients often have differences both 137 in the presence of disease manifestations (some late-onset FD patients may only have renal 138 disease or only cardiac disease) and in the rate of disease progression. Given the multisystemic 139 nature of FD, the highly variable rate of disease progression (especially in late-onset FD patients 140 and in female patients), and the heterogeneity of clinical manifestations, sponsors could consider 141 combining multiple clinical outcomes for assessment in clinical trials. Specifically, sponsors 142 could consider the use of a composite endpoint such that changes in symptoms and/or functional 143 outcomes could be captured across a variety of FD manifestations. The choice of such endpoints 144 could be based on baseline symptom presence and severity in enrolled patients. FDA strongly 145 encourages sponsors to engage in early discussions (as early as the pre-investigational new drug 146

candidates.statement: Sponsors can establish drug effectiveness with the demonstration of clinically meaningful 154 improvement in neuropathic symptoms, including pain, or gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal 155 pain, diarrhea, constipation). Sponsors should select well-defined and reliable instruments for 156 assessments of changes in such symptoms in accordance with the recommendations of the 157 guidance for industry Patient-Reported Outcome Measures: Use in Medical Product 158 Development to Support Labeling Claims (December 2009). FDA strongly encourages sponsors 159 to engage early with the appropriate review division for selection of the most appropriate clinical 160 outcome assessment instruments. FDA encourages the development of publicly available, fit-for- 161 purpose, patient-reported outcome instruments that can be used across multiple drug 162 development programs in FD to facilitate and accelerate drug development in this disease. 14

Neuropathic and gastrointestinal symptoms 152 13 The term traditional approval denotes the longstanding route of drug approval based on the demonstration of clinical benefit or an effect on a surrogate endpoint known to predict clinical benefit. That term is distinguished from accelerated approval, which is associated with use of a surrogate endpoint or intermediate clinical endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit to support drug approval.

candidates.statement: Sponsors could use the demonstration of a sustained treatment effect on a specified magnitude of 167 loss of renal function (e.g., a 30 percent decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR), assessed via 168 a widely accepted estimating equation for GFR or measured GFR) or on the rate of loss of renal 169 function as the basis for traditional drug approval. In general, sponsors of trials using rate of loss 170 of renal function as an endpoint (e.g., a comparison of the annualized change in estimated GFR 171 (eGFR) between the treatment arms) should assess whether the treatment effect continues to 172 accrue across the various stages of renal disease by enrolling patients with different levels of 173 renal function at baseline. In addition, the trial duration should be sufficient (generally at least 24 174 months) to evaluate for long-term effectiveness and to obtain a more reliable estimate of the 175 treatment effect on the rate of change in eGFR. 176
candidates.context: In general, programs should collect information on progression to end-stage renal disease 178 requiring chronic dialysis or renal transplantation while acknowledging that such events are 179 likely to be uncommon in clinical trials of early-stage renal disease in FD given the slowly 180 progressive nature of FD. 181

candidates.statement: Sponsors can use histological reduction of GL-3 inclusion burden in biopsied kidney interstitial 183 capillaries (KIC) as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit to support 184 accelerated approval. If a sponsor plans to use a surrogate endpoint based on histological 185 assessment of GL-3 inclusions, FDA encourages the sponsor to engage in early discussion with 186 the appropriate review division to more precisely define such an endpoint (including the 187 magnitude of change in that endpoint) that would be reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. 188 When assessing (counting) KIC GL-3 inclusions in histology specimens, the sponsor should use 189 validated and standardized assay methodologies, and scoring of KIC GL-3 inclusions should be 190 conducted by experienced pathologists in a blinded and systematic fashion. In general, 191 postmarketing studies to verify and describe the clinical benefit should already be underway at 192 the time of submission of a marketing application. FDA encourages sponsors to engage in early 193 discussion with the appropriate review division regarding trial design features of such 194 postmarketing studies. 195
